## ACTIONABLE

### D1. MathOverflow: the (72,108) exclusion + ≥125 bound have been public consensus on the
### canonical JC(2) thread since Jul 23 — with an anonymous "write-up in preparation"
New-to-us (not new-to-world); found on the first-ever MO sweep, and it closes yesterday's open
carry-over ("locate the MO thread implied by Strinz's Jul 28 correction").

Thread: **Q513413 "The simplest case of Jacobian conjecture"** (asked Jul 21, score 47, last
activity Jul 28 — exactly the date of Strinz's retraction commit).
https://mathoverflow.net/questions/513413

- **Answer https://mathoverflow.net/a/513493 by "ratto3423" (Jul 23, score 13):** states, precisely,
  that GGHV 2204.14178 reduces everything below 125 to (72,108); that after the paper's own (9,27)
  exclusion only two supports remain at the (8,28) corner (Prop. 4.3); that "a computer-assisted
  calculation eliminates both", giving max(deg P, deg Q) ≥ 125 over any algebraically closed field
  of char 0 — ending with "**Write-up in preparation**".
- **Top answer (KConrad, score 55) was edited Jul 24 to endorse it**: "another answer on this page
  improves the lower bound on the degree to 125." So the ≥125 planar floor is not just a Zenodo
  artifact chain — it is community-visible knowledge on the highest-traffic JC(2) thread, and has
  been for ~26 days.
- **ratto3423 is a single-purpose throwaway**: account created 2026-07-23 (same day as the answer),
  rep 141, exactly one post ever, no profile info, no follow-up edit since Jul 23.
- Identity hypotheses: (a) **Helali** under a pseudonym — timeline (Zenodo live Jul 21, answer
  Jul 23 = his last GitHub-active day) and content (both (8,28)-corner systems eliminated by exact
  computation) match his artifact exactly; the "write-up" would be a paper version of 21479814.
  (b) A **fifth, unknown actor** with an independent computation and a pending paper. Strinz is
  unlikely to be the author (published under his own name Jul 24; his Jul 28 correction retracted
  claims *about* "MathOverflow answers and a pull request", i.e. he had referenced this answer, not
  written it — the "pull request" half of that retraction remains unlocated).

**Why this matters (borderline URGENT):** (1) Paper-1 timing — an unidentified party declared a
formal write-up of exactly our settled case 26 days ago; nothing has surfaced on arXiv/Zenodo since,
but if it lands first it takes the paper-of-record slot for the (72,108) exclusion. (2) Paper-1
citations — the priority chain should now read Helali (Zenodo, Jul 21) → ratto3423 (MO a/513493,
Jul 23, anonymous) → Strinz (Zenodo, Jul 24) → Ishihara (Aug 2) → us (Aug 11); the MO answer is
citable and reviewers WILL know the thread (KConrad's edit guarantees it). (3) Monitoring — add a
standing arXiv/Zenodo watch for any new (72,108)/degree-125 write-up; that is now the single most
important tripwire for this campaign.

## CONTEXT

### D2. MO Q514380 "About AI and how we publish" (Aug 17, score 21, 6 answers) — new meta-thread;
### registry infrastructure for AI claims is being built in public
https://mathoverflow.net/questions/514380 (Joaquin Lema). No JC(2)/(72,108) content. Relevant to us
anyway: Philip Weiss (answer) is building **TheoremDB** — "infrastructure for recording open problems
and candidate results... attaching Lean certificates"; another answer (B K) proposes a catalogue of
AI-solved conjectures (paper link + model + solution + prompts). Together with openconjectures.org,
these are the venues where a plane-case claim like ours would get registered/tracked. Companion
thread Q514181 ("LLM-generated counterexample", Aug 12, score 41) is about a real-rootedness
conjecture, not JC; Timothy Chow's top-voted stance ("chances are pretty high it is correct...
adversarial audit... Lean") is a useful marker of shifting community norms toward artifact-backed
AI claims. Watch-only; possible future action: register our artifact in such a registry once Paper 1
is out.
